title: The survey that broke the rules
instructions:
## You are on the departmental ethics committee

A final-year student submits a project proposal: a survey of students' use of AI tools, with interviews. Read the proposal extract and decide what must change before it can run.

evidence.title: Proposal extract
evidence.text: Method: a Google Form sent to all level 300 WhatsApp groups, collecting name, index number, programme and answers. Participation is compulsory for students in my hall. Interviews recorded on my phone. Data kept on my laptop. Results will name students with the most interesting answers so lecturers can follow up.

choices.feedback: Several rules are broken: compulsion, identification, storage and disclosure.

choices.text: Participation must be voluntary with informed consent, and nobody may be made to take part
choices.feedback: Correct. Voluntary, informed consent is the first requirement of research with people.
Every data collection needs consent, including the form.

nodes.title: Identification
nodes.text: The form collects names and index numbers. What should change?

choices.text: Collect no identifiers unless they are needed; if interviews need contact, keep the key separate and anonymise the data
choices.feedback: Correct. Minimise identifiers and separate them from the answers.

choices.text: Keep the names; they make the data richer
choices.feedback: Names add risk, not insight, for this question.
Phone numbers identify people just as well.

nodes.title: Disclosure
nodes.text: The student plans to name students with "interesting answers" to lecturers. This is:

choices.text: A breach of confidentiality that could harm participants, and must be removed
choices.feedback: Correct. Participants must not be exposed to consequences from what they told the researcher.
The lecturers are not the ones at risk.

choices.text: Acceptable if the answers are positive
choices.feedback: The participant decides what is disclosed, not the researcher.

nodes.title: Storage
nodes.text: Recordings on a personal phone and data on a laptop. What is required?

choices.text: Encrypted storage, access limited to the researcher and supervisor, and deletion of recordings once transcribed and anonymised
choices.feedback: Correct. Secure storage and a retention plan are part of the protocol.

choices.text: Nothing; it is the student's own device
choices.feedback: The data belongs to the participants' privacy, not the device owner.

choices.text: Upload everything to a public drive for transparency
choices.feedback: Transparency applies to methods and aggregate results, not personal data.

nodes.title: Sampling
nodes.text: Only the student's hall WhatsApp groups receive the form. For a claim about "level 300 students", this is:

choices.text: A convenience sample with selection bias; the claim must be limited or the sampling improved
choices.feedback: Correct. The sample does not represent the population the claim is about.
Random sampling gives every member a known chance; hall groups do not.
Popularity of the channel is not representativeness of the sample.

nodes.title: Decision: revise and resubmit
nodes.text: The committee requires voluntary consent, no identifiers, no disclosure of individual answers, secure storage with deletion, and either a better sampling frame or a narrower claim.

hints: Collect only what the question needs.
A sample must come from the population the claim is about.

checks.label: At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: University ethics committees in Ghana review exactly these points, and the Data Protection Act applies to student research as much as to companies.
